lines.plain: فاكرين ريحة الحلو مر في الحوش؟
lines.vocalized: فَاكْرِين رِيحَة الْحِلُو مُرّ فِي الْحَوْشْ؟
lines.en: Remember the smell of hilu-murr in the courtyard?

lines.plain: والبروش في الشارع، وكل بيت يخرج صينيته..
lines.vocalized: وَالْبُرُوش فِي الشَّارِعْ، وَكُلّ بَيْت يُخْرِج صِينِيَّتَهْ..
lines.en: The mats out in the street, and every house bringing out its tray...
The family gathered... and the little ones waiting for Maghrib.

lines.plain: لكن منذ الحرب، ترك كثير من أهلنا بيوتهم.
lines.vocalized: لَكِنْ مُنْذُ الْحَرْبْ، تَرَكَ كَثِير مِنْ أَهْلِنَا بُيُوتَهُمْ.
lines.en: But since the war, many of our people have left their homes.

lines.plain: ورمضان هذا، لم تعد صينيتهم زي زمان.
lines.vocalized: وَرَمَضَان هَذَا، لَمْ تَعُدْ صِينِيَّتُهُمْ زَيّ زَمَانْ.
lines.en: And this Ramadan, their tray is not what it was in the old days.

lines.plain: ولكي تمتلئ الصينية من جديد.. هذه مبادرة حقيبة رمضان.
lines.vocalized: وَلِكَيْ تَمْتَلِئ الصِّينِيَّة مِنْ جَدِيدْ.. هَذِهِ مُبَادَرَة حَقِيبَة رَمَضَانْ.
lines.en: So the tray can be full again... this is the Ramadan Bag Initiative.

lines.plain: حقيبة واحدة تكفي أسرة من ستة أفراد.. لأسبوعين.
lines.vocalized: حَقِيبَة وَاحِدَة تَكْفِي أُسْرَة مِنْ سِتَّة أَفْرَادْ.. لِأُسْبُوعَيْنْ.
lines.en: One bag is enough for a family of six... for two weeks.

lines.plain: وحقها كم؟ ما يعادل خمسين دولارًا.
lines.vocalized: وَحَقَّهَا كَمْ؟ مَا يُعَادِل خَمْسِين دُولَارًا.
lines.en: And how much is it? The equivalent of fifty dollars.

lines.plain: زي زمان.. شاركوا صينيتكم مع أهلنا، وساهموا معنا بحقيبة.
lines.vocalized: زَيّ زَمَانْ.. شَارِكُوا صِينِيَّتَكُمْ مَعَ أَهْلِنَا، وَسَاهِمُوا مَعَنَا بِحَقِيبَةْ.
lines.en: Like the old days... share your tray with our people, and give a bag with us.

lines.plain: ولا داعي أن تحملوها وحدكم.. اجمعوا قيمتها مع الأهل والحبان.
lines.vocalized: وَلَا دَاعِي أَنْ تَحْمِلُوهَا وَحْدَكُمْ.. اِجْمَعُوا قِيمَتَهَا مَعَ الْأَهْل وَالْحُبَّانْ.
lines.en: You don't have to carry it alone... pool its cost with family and loved ones.
In Sudanese pounds: Bankak or Fawry.

lines.plain: ومن خارج مصر: تحويل بنكي، أو ويسترن يونيون.
lines.vocalized: وَمِنْ خَارِج مِصْرْ: تَحْوِيل بَنْكِيّ، أَوْ ويسترن يونيون.
lines.en: From outside Egypt: bank transfer, or Western Union.

lines.plain: بعد الدفع، صوروا الشاشة.. وأرسلوا لنا الإشعار على الواتساب.
lines.vocalized: بَعْد الدَّفْعْ، صَوِّرُوا الشَّاشَةْ.. وَأَرْسِلُوا لَنَا الْإِشْعَار عَلَى الواتساب.
lines.en: After paying, take a screenshot... and send us the transfer notice on WhatsApp.

lines.plain: الخير ما بكتر بمال زول واحد،
lines.vocalized: الخير مَا بِكْتَر بِمَال زُول وَاحِدْ،
lines.en: Goodness doesn't grow from one person's money,

lines.plain: الخير بكتر بقلوب كتيرة اجتمعت على المحبة والعطاء.
lines.vocalized: الخير بِكْتَر بِقُلُوب كَتِيرَة اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَى الْمَحَبَّة وَالْعَطَاءْ.
lines.en: goodness grows from many hearts brought together by love and giving.

[slowly] الخير مَا بِكْتَر بِمَال زُول وَاحِدْ، [pause]

rationale:
SPINE: Draft B. It is the most even hybrid. The middle of the script uses warm, plain fusha for its verbs, negation and connectives (لم تعد، لكي، لا داعي). The opener and the price question now go back to the original's Sudanese/common colloquial: «فاكرين ريحة…» and «وحقها كم؟». So the first three seconds sound like a family voice, not a documentary, and the Sudanese touches run across the whole arc instead of sitting only at the two ends. The verb choices are also the safest for TTS. It uses شاركوا instead of أخرجوا, which TTS can misread as "get out!", and it includes Western Union and بعد الدفع.

GRAFTS:
(1) From A and C, beat 2 brings back البروش, the Sudanese mats image. I dropped الضرا because its pronunciation is uncertain and risky for TTS, and wrote «والبروش في الشارع».
(2) From A and C, beat 3 uses الصغار instead of الأطفال. It is warmer and avoids الشفع. The kids now wait for «المغرب» only. I dropped «أذان» because it added about 3 syllables and no meaning in a 3.0s beat.
(3) Beat 4 is closer to the original «خلوا بيوتهم»: «ترك كثير من أهلنا بيوتهم». It is gentle and non-political.
(4) The original script's «ما زي زمان → زي زمان» echo is restored. Beat 5 says their tray is no longer «زيّ زمان», and beat 9 answers with «زيّ زمان.. شاركوا صينيتكم». That is the persuasive hinge of the piece.
(5) From B, beat 10 keeps الحُبّان as the Sudanese term of warmth.
(6) The opener is the original's hook in hybrid form: «فاكرين ريحة الحلو مُر في الحوش؟». It replaces the textbook «هل تذكرون رائحة». فاكرين and ريحة are common across dialects, and TTS reads them reliably.
(7) The price beat is now «وحقها كم؟ ما يعادل خمسين دولارًا.». The Sudanese question is much shorter than «وكم قيمتها؟», and «ما يعادل» keeps the 'equivalent' fact.
(8) Beat 6 says «هذه مبادرة حقيبة رمضان» instead of «جاءت…». The line no longer suggests the initiative was founded because of the war, which the fact sheet does not say.
I dropped A's «وكما نقول في السودان:» lead-in because it would put 10 words in 3.0s.

THE HYBRID MIX: light fusha grammar, plus Sudanese openers and nouns: فاكرين ريحة، الحلو مُرّ، الحوش، البروش، لمّة، الصينية ×4، أهلنا ×3، وحقها كم، الحُبّان. زيّ زمان appears twice, and the poster proverb is kept word for word in Sudanese. The proverb keeps the poster's comma between its halves, and a [pause] tag gives the breath.

FACTS: everything comes from the fact sheet. That covers the name, 6 people for two weeks, the equivalent of 50 dollars, Bankak or Fawry for Sudanese pounds, InstaPay for Egyptian pounds, and bank transfer or Western Union from outside Egypt. The WhatsApp notice comes after paying. No IBAN, account number, SWIFT code or phone number is spoken. The war gets one short line.

WORD COUNT: 115 spoken words. The densest beats are 41.5-44.5 (8 words in 3.0s), 17.0-21.5, 21.5-24.9, 27.4-32.0 and 32.0-36.4. If 41.5-44.5 runs long, keep «من خارج مصر». That wording is the fact: «من الخارج» would include Egypt, where the right route is InstaPay. Trim the pauses instead, for example «وخارج مصر: تحويل بنكي أو ويسترن يونيون», which drops «ومن» and the comma. You can also borrow a little time from 44.5-48.5. If the middle runs long overall, use the roughly 2s of slack in the proverb beat.

TASHKEEL CONVENTIONS:
- Light fusha. Internal vowels are marked, but tanween and case or mood endings are dropped in the middle of phrases: كَثِير، بَيْت، كُلّ، حَقِيبَة وَاحِدَة، أُسْرَة، سِتَّة أَفْرَادْ، تَحْوِيل، يُخْرِج، يَنْتَظِرُون، يُعَادِل، خَمْسِين، تَمْتَلِئ الصِّينِيَّة، مُبَادَرَة حَقِيبَة رَمَضَانْ، دَاعِي، بَعْد، الْإِشْعَار، بِالْجُنَيْه. This shortens the read and keeps TTS out of a news-bulletin register. Built-in endings stay (مُنْذُ، تَرَكَ، مَعَ، هَذِهِ). So do vowels before attached pronouns (بُيُوتَهُمْ، صِينِيَّتَكُمْ، قِيمَتَهَا، وَحْدَكُمْ).
- Pausal sukun on the last word before every comma, ellipsis, question mark and full stop. I also applied it at colons (السُّودَانِيّ: / مِصْرْ:) because a narrator pauses there too.
- دُولَارًا keeps its tanween, as instructed. It is the only tanween in the script.
- Shadda on every geminate. That includes sun-letter assimilation (الشَّارِع، الصِّينِيَّة، الصِّغَار، الدَّفْع، الشَّاشَة), كُلّ، حَقَّهَا، and نِسبة endings at pause (بَنْكِيّ، المِصْرِيّ). The colloquial «like» is written زَيّ, with no vowel after the shadda, because this Sudanese word takes no case ending.
- Hamzat al-wasl is left bare in the middle of a phrase so TTS links it without a glottal stop (كَتِيرَة اجْتَمَعَتْ). It carries a kasra only at the start of an utterance (اِجْمَعُوا after the ellipsis). It is written as a bare ا, never ٱ.
- Moon-letter lam carries sukun.
- I left the dagger alif out of لَكِنْ، هَذَا and هَذِهِ because TTS knows those words and may not render the superscript mark.
- Sudanese words are vocalized the Sudanese way: فَاكْرِين، رِيحَة، الْحِلُو مُرّ، زَيّ زَمَانْ، حَقَّهَا كَمْ، الْحُبَّان، بِكْتَر، زُول، كَتِيرَة، وَاحِدْ.
- الخير is left unmarked. ق in بِقُلُوب and حَقَّهَا is read as written.
- Foreign brand names stay in Arabic script without tashkeel: إنستا باي، ويسترن يونيون، الواتساب. بَنْكَك and فَوْرِي are marked so they read Bankak and Fawry.

CHECK ON THE FIRST TAKE:
- Time the take beat by beat against the grid, starting with the dense beats listed above.
- الحَوْش will come out "hawsh" rather than the Sudanese "hosh". That is acceptable.
- If الحُبَّان misfires, use الأحباب.
- If إنستا باي or ويسترن يونيون sound off, try the Latin InstaPay and Western Union.
- If the proverb comes out too fusha, generate beats 48.5-57.0 as a separate slower take.
- 57.0-60.0 stays music only with the end card. It is left out of the lines so the TTS never reads a stage direction.
